notes.text: Overnight bags only today: the suitcases should already be at Kujō House. Message the host before you leave Hakone to check they arrived.
Tō-ji and the Hozenji bars are cash territory. Hit a konbini ATM in Odawara or Kyoto Station, not mid-market.
December cold all day, dark before you even reach Osaka. Layers and gloves for an outdoor market and a night of alley-hopping.

stops.summary: Out the door with overnight bags; two pre-booked taxis beat a three-hour bus slog to Odawara.
stops.story: Public transport off the mountain means changes and waiting at cold bus stops; two taxis drop you at the castle in 37 min. It's the difference between seeing Odawara and seeing a bus shelter.
how: Book two taxis through the villa the night before.
Be out by 09:30 with overnight bags only.
Split four and four, meet at the castle gate.
tips: Do a sweep for chargers and passports: the villa is a long way back.
stops.booking: Two taxis via the villa, the night before
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: A white samurai keep over Sagami Bay, then ekiben and beers for the bullet train.
stops.story: Odawara's rebuilt keep stands over a winter-bare garden, with a floor of samurai armour and a top-floor lookout across Sagami Bay. It's a quick, cold, very photogenic hit before the train west.
how: Head straight up the keep; save the grounds for the walk out.
Armour floor, then the viewing deck at the top.
Walk 14 min to Odawara Station and raid the ekiben stands and beer fridges.
tips: Admission was revised in 2026: check the price at the gate (it was ¥1,000).
Hours were 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30; check on the day.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: Kodama to Shizuoka, Hikari to Kyoto: ekiben lunch, beers and Fuji out the right-hand window.
stops.story: This leg is on full fare, not a pass, so make it count: crack the beers, eat the ekiben and watch for Fuji after Odawara. Clear winter air is your best shot at the snow-capped cone.
how: Kodama 11:42 to Shizuoka (12:31).
Change to the Hikari 12:49, into Kyoto 14:26.
At Kyoto, coin-locker the bags, then walk 11 min to Tō-ji.
tips: Grab right-hand window seats for Fuji.
Not on the Kansai-Hiroshima pass: that starts tomorrow.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.summary: The last flea market of the year: 1,000+ stalls of vintage kimono and junk under a giant pagoda.
stops.story: Shimai-Kōbō is the year's final Kōbō-san, when Tō-ji's grounds fill with vintage kimono, antiques, New Year food and street snacks around Japan's tallest wooden pagoda. You're catching the tail end, so prices loosen as sellers start packing up.
how: Split into fours, cash in hand.
Sweep for vintage haori and kimono, then eat your way through the snack stalls.
Regroup at the pagoda before the light goes.
tips: It winds down from 16:00, so start with the stall you'd regret skipping.
wishes: Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls

stops.summary: Reunite with the suitcases, shower, change, and pocket the original passports for the night.
stops.story: First night at the Osaka base, with the suitcases waiting from Tokyo. Fast turnaround, then straight back out to Minami.
how: Find the TA-Q-BIN suitcases and check all 8 arrived.
Showers in shifts, then out the door.
Original passports on every person.
tips: Leave by 18:36 for the Hanshin train toward Namba.
wishes: Osaka base, but during the day we will commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed

stops.summary: Eight courses of poisonous pufferfish, done properly, with two hours of drinks and flaming fin sake.
stops.story: Winter tora-fugu is the whole tour: paper-thin tessa sashimi, tecchiri hot-pot, fugu karaage and the porridge finish in the leftover broth. The fin sake comes hot, smoky and lethal in a different way.
how: Course: Fuyu no Utage, 8 courses with 2h nomihōdai and fin sake.
Tessa first, eaten a few slices at a time with ponzu.
Save room: the porridge is the best bit.
tips: Check the booking time: Plan C said 19:30, today's plan says 19:00.
stops.booking: Hot Pepper, 8-course winter course for 8 (check the reservation)
wishes: Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)

stops.summary: Splash water on a moss-furred Fudō statue for luck, then a drink in pairs in the lantern alley.
stops.story: One minute from the Dotonbori chaos, a stone alley goes quiet under paper lanterns, and Fudō-san is so soaked in wishes he's grown a coat of moss. The bars are tiny, so this works in small squads.
how: Ladle water onto Fudō-san and make a wish.
Split up: most bars seat 4–6.
Regroup at the statue.
tips: Some bars add an otoshi seat charge of ¥300–500.
Hours vary by shop: if it's dark, try the next one.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly

stops.summary: Two squads of four hop the standing bars and yakiton counters where young Osaka actually drinks.
stops.story: Ura-Namba is a grid of standing bars, horumon and yakiton counters behind Namba, cheap and packed close enough to hop every drink. Osaka Yakiton Center kicked off the boom; Ankeraso does all horumon at ¥330.
how: Two squads of four, one or two drinks per stop.
Standing-bar drinks run ¥400–600.
Walk to Osaka-Namba for the 23:56 Hanshin to Kujō (00:03).
tips: Monday is the easy night: later in the week bonenkai crowds fill bars.
Miss the 23:56 and it's a taxi: 16 min to Kujō.
Home by midnight: Fushimi Inari is at first light.
wishes: Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
